LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words do we use to describe people, things, and places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly
2. use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 ADJECTIVES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 ADJECTIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives to a partner. (skill: use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly.
3. Practise this skill: use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words do we use to describe people, things, and places?
2. How do we compare people, things, and events?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Adjectives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in print and digital texts correctly.
5. Be able to: use simple, comparative and superlative forms of adjectives in oral and written texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
